column1: # web/e2e/areas.tsv — which feature spec a changed source path makes necessary.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR. The `e2e-builder`/`e2e-core` preflight gates run the whole
# feature family on a default run. A `--for-diff <base-ref>` run narrows them to
# the specs this file maps, so a release pays for the areas it touched instead of
# the whole suite (measured 2026-11-10: the family costs ~570s, 21% of a release
# run). This file is DATA, not code: the matcher is
# `web/scripts/e2e-scope.mjs`, and it is re-checked by `scripts/spec-counts.sh`
# (the `speccounts` gate) so a spec that arrives without a row cannot silently
# fall out of the narrowed set.
# FORMAT. TAB separated, one row per line:
#     <spec-glob>  <area-glob>  [<area-glob> ...]
# * `spec-glob` is matched against the spec's BASENAME (`builder-save-failure.spec.ts`).
#   A `*` spec-glob marks a GLOBAL area: any changed path matching it selects the
#   WHOLE family, because it is shared by specs this file cannot enumerate.
# * `area-glob` is matched against the changed path as git reports it, i.e. from
#   the repo root (`web/src/app/sales/page.tsx`). `**` spans directories.
# * Blank lines and `#` lines are ignored.
# THE RULES THAT MAKE NARROWING SAFE (implemented in `e2e-scope.mjs`, asserted by
# its `--self-test`):
#   1. A change to a spec file selects that spec.
#   2. A change to any source path the spec NAMES (`src/...` inside its own
#      text — the import it drives) selects that spec. This is derived, not
#      typed here, so a shared helper the spec imports cannot be missed by a row.
#   3. A change to a path matched by a row's area globs selects that row's spec.
#   4. ANY OTHER changed path under `web/` selects the WHOLE family — UNLESS the
#      TREE attributes it (rule 4a). A change nothing can attribute might still
#      reach any spec, so it is never narrowed away.
#   4a. DERIVED attribution (card t_902bd1f7) — a new page, and a screenshot under
#      `web/public/`, used to match no row at all, so a docs diff ran BOTH families
#      in full (measured on PR #1701: 2359s of browser work, e2e-core's only red on
#      a page no spec visits). A path the map does not claim is instead derived
#      from the tree: a `web/public/` asset -> the page(s) whose source names its
#      URL -> the route(s) they serve; any other `web/src/` module -> the route(s)
#      of the page(s) that import it; a `web/scripts/` file -> inert when no npm
#      script in the build/start chain runs it. Only the specs whose own text
#      names that route run, and NONE means ZERO (the gate prints NOT RUN). It
#      widens back to the whole family when the route is named by code serving a
#      DIFFERENT route, when an e2e helper names it, when the route cannot be
#      spelled statically (`[param]`, a route handler, the root route), or when
#      the tree cannot be read — the fail-closed valve stays ON; what is switched
#      off is only the assumption that an unattributable path is unknowable.
#   5. A feature spec with NO row here selects the WHOLE family (the family's
#      coverage is not knowable, so it is not narrowed).
#   6. `web/playwright.config.ts`, `web/playwright.menufixture.config.ts`, this
#      file, and every non-spec file under `web/e2e/` (the shared helpers) select
#      the WHOLE family.
# So the file can only ever make a run SMALLER when a change is positively
# attributed. Getting a row wrong costs coverage of one area; leaving a path
# unclaimed costs the whole family's run time, never coverage.
# SPECS OWNED BY ANOTHER GATE HAVE NO ROW HERE (card t_440c9417, option B: one owner
# per test). A spec can live under web/e2e/ and still not belong to this family:
# `menu-checkout-option-group.spec.ts` needs the `menufixture` Go server
# (MENU_FIXTURE_URL, api/cmd/menu-fixture), which these gates' `next start` cannot
# serve, so `web/playwright.config.ts` testIgnore's it and the `menufixture` gate is
# its ONLY runner. The matcher excludes it by name (`OTHER_GATE_SPECS` in
# web/scripts/e2e-scope.mjs, which is also where the declaration is checked against
# the tree); a diff that touches only it decides a subset of ZERO, so the e2e gates
# print NOT RUN — never a spec path handed to a project that does not enumerate it,
# which runs nothing and would read as a pass.
# THE BLIND SPOT, NAMED. A narrowed run does not exercise a spec whose area the
# diff did not touch, and the printed decision line says so (`e2e-core: 41/76
# specs`) — it is never reported as the full family. `PREFLIGHT_E2E=full` forces
# every spec on any run, and that is the run a release card must quote as full.
# ---- GLOBAL: shared by the whole family, so any change selects all of it ----
